item.title: From prison to presidency: Madagascar’s coup leader sworn in as president – who is Colonel Michael Randrianirina?
item.description: Colonel Michael Randrianirina, once imprisoned for an attempted mutiny, has assumed Madagascar’s presidency after ousting Andry Rajoelina, who fled amid widespread Gen Z-led protests over chronic power and water shortages. Leading his elite CAPSAT unit, Randrianirina seized momentum from the unrest to enforce a transitional military-civilian governance of up to two years, projecting disciplined, pragmatic leadership focused on patriotism, social welfare, and national unity.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: CEO killer Luigi Mangione’s lawyers claim Trump administration is 'using him as a pawn' to advance its own agenda
item.description: Defense attorneys argue that public comments from President Trump and Attorney General Pam Bondi have prejudiced the case of a 27-year-old man charged with murder. They claim these statements, along with UnitedHealthcare's lobbying efforts, unfairly portray the defendant as the sole villain, jeopardizing his right to a fair trial.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: FBI arrests Louisiana man; accuses him of providing materials to Hamas in deadly October 7 Israel attack — Who is Al-Muhtadi?
item.description: A suspect, Mahmoud Amin Ya-qub Al-Muhtadi, was arrested in Louisiana for allegedly participating in Hamas's October 7, 2023, attack on Israel. Court documents accuse him of providing material support to a foreign terrorist organization and visa fraud. He is alleged to have armed himself, recruited others, and entered Israel near a massacre site.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Before Justin-Katy romance, Trudeau's father once dated a famous singer; ‘It’s in their DNA’
item.description: Canadian ex-PM Justin Trudeau was reportedly seen with pop star Katy Perry on a yacht, sparking comparisons to his father, Pierre Trudeau. Pierre had a notable romance with singer-actress Barbra Streisand in the late 1960s. Both father and son appear drawn to famous partners and public attention, echoing a familial pattern.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Zohran Mamdani accuses Andrew Cuomo of ignoring Muslims: 'Name a single mosque'
item.description: Democratic mayoral candidate Zohran Mamdani criticized former Governor Andrew Cuomo for neglecting the Muslim community during his tenure. Mamdani asserted that Cuomo only visited a mosque after being challenged by a Muslim candidate, highlighting a perceived lack of engagement. Cuomo defended his record, citing past work with the community. The debate also touched on housing and other key issues.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Continued accusations about me distract Majesty': Prince Andrew gives up his royal titles and honours
item.description: Prince Andrew has relinquished his Duke of York title amidst ongoing criticism over his associations with Jeffrey Epstein and a business associate suspected of being a Chinese spy. He stated his decision was to avoid distracting from King Charles's work and the wider royal family.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'He looks beautiful': Trump gives thumps up to Zelenskyy's outfit — Watch
item.description: President Trump praised Ukrainian President Zelenskyy's stylish dark suit during their White House meeting, a stark contrast to his earlier teasing of Zelenskyy's military attire. The discussion focused on Ukraine's request for Tomahawk missiles, while Trump also announced plans for a second summit with Russian President Putin.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A ‘smug’ Mamdani, a ‘sickly’ Cuomo, and a ‘relaxed’ Sliwa: Body language expert decodes NYC mayoral debate
item.description: Body language expert Carole Lieberman analyzed the NYC mayoral debate, noting Zohran Mamdani's "clenched jaw and erratic hand gestures" suggested a desire to appear tough. Former Governor Andrew Cuomo appeared "bedraggled" and "worried," while Curtis Sliwa was described as the "most relaxed and friendly."
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘No Kings’ protest returns nationwide, millions expected to march against Trump’s ‘abuse of power’ — What we all know
item.description: Millions are expected to participate in the second edition of the "No Kings" protests nationwide, organized by groups like the ACLU, against President Trump's administration. Celebrities are lending their support. Republicans have criticized the rallies, with some labeling them "Hate America" events, while organizers emphasize peaceful demonstration and democratic rights.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Verdict of Americans': Trump dubbed the 'peace president' as poll shows highest approval, Obama and Biden fall short
item.description: A new Daily Mail poll suggests Donald Trump is perceived by American voters as having done more for Middle East peace than his four immediate predecessors combined. Voters credited him with brokering a historic Middle East deal, surpassing even Nobel Peace Prize winner Barack Obama in recognition for peace efforts.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Riyadh to Jeddah in 4 hours: Saudi Arabia Railways reaches critical stage in $7 billion Landbridge project"
item.description: Saudi Arabia is building a massive new railway network. The ambitious plans aim to connect cities and ports, boosting trade and travel. A key project, the Landbridge, will link Jeddah to Dammam. This expansion is part of Vision 2030, transforming the kingdom into a major transport hub for the region.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Three indictments, one exception: Why the case of John Bolton stands apart from that of James Comey and Letitia James
item.description: In a rapid sequence of politically charged prosecutions, President Trump’s Justice Department has indicted John Bolton, James Comey, and Letitia James. Bolton, who surrendered to authorities on October 17, 2025, and pleaded not guilty to eighteen counts involving classified national-security material, faces the gravest stakes. While all three critics call the charges politically motivated, Bolton’s indictment intertwines legal accountability with profound implications for US national security.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Will Prince Andrew lose his royal title after Epstein bombshell? Here's what report said
item.description: Prince Andrew faces potential loss of his Duke of York title as palace insiders consider "all options" to resolve the ongoing sex abuse scandal. New emails reveal he maintained contact with Jeffrey Epstein, contradicting previous claims. Palace officials are reportedly "frustrated and exasperated," hoping Andrew "does the decent thing" before decisive measures are implemented.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: What’s happening this weekend in Dubai: Top 5 things to do, from Diwali fireworks to supercar rides!
item.description: Dubai is set to host a vibrant weekend from October 17-19 with diverse events for all. From theatrical performances like Slava's SNOWSHOW to electrifying music acts including LOBODA and Robin Schulz, there's something for everyone. The city also offers stand-up comedy, luxury experiences, sports, and grand Diwali celebrations with fireworks.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Between Death and Tteokbokki: The life and legacy of Baek Se-hee
item.description: Baek Se-hee's memoir, "I Want to Die but I Want to Eat Tteokbokki," offered a radical, honest record of therapy sessions, resonating globally. Her vulnerability in sharing her struggles with depression became a cultural rupture, giving language to a generation's quiet despair and redefining resilience as persistence through simple pleasures.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: After Mitch McConnell trips and falls, social media trolls Nancy Pelosi over her previous tumble: 'Both need to retire'
item.description: Kentucky Senator Mitch McConnell, 83, collapsed in the Capitol basement shortly after being questioned about ICE. He was helped up by security and a Capitol Police officer and was en route to vote on spending bills. The incident has sparked discussions about the physical demands of public office for elderly lawmakers.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 2025 UAE update: Key changes for private sector employees on working hours, overtime, pay, and leave
item.description: The UAE Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation has announced new rules for private sector workers. These clarifications cover working hours, overtime pay, and various types of leave. The aim is to ensure fair treatment and transparency for all employees. Employers and workers can now better understand their rights and responsibilities.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UAE announces new category for Golden Visa: Secure 10-year residency through Waqf donations
item.description: The UAE has introduced a 10-year Golden Visa for donors to Islamic Waqf endowments, recognizing their contributions to humanitarian work. This initiative, a collaboration between GDRFA-Dubai and Awqaf Dubai, aims to attract global philanthropists and position the UAE as a hub for generosity and sustainable development.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: John Bolton indictment: Ex-Trump adviser surrenders in mishandling classified information case — all you need to know
item.description: Former National Security Adviser John Bolton surrendered Friday to face charges of mishandling classified information. The indictment alleges he shared sensitive intelligence notes with his wife and daughter for a book, violating the Espionage Act. Bolton denies wrongdoing, vowing to fight the charges and expose alleged presidential abuse of power.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
